faq.a: A short, step-by-step plan that connects tools you already use, such as your phone system, booking app or Google Sheets, with an AI step to save time on a repetitive task.

pages.label: HVAC
pages.title: Text back every missed call automatically for an HVAC business
pages.summary: When a call is missed during a job, send an automatic text asking for the address and issue, log the reply, and alert the on-call tech.
steps: Connect your business phone system (a VoIP service such as OpenPhone, Dialpad or a Twilio number) so it fires a webhook or Zapier trigger on missed calls.
In Zapier, Make or n8n, send an SMS: “Sorry we missed you — this is {Company}. Reply with your address and the issue (no heat / no cool / maintenance) and we'll call back within the hour.”
Log every reply to your CRM or a Google Sheet.
Forward the reply to the on-call technician's phone.

p: Tools: Phone system webhook → Zapier/Make/n8n → SMS → Sheet/CRM. Costs: see each vendor's current pricing page.
SMS consent rules (TCPA and 10DLC registration in the US): only text numbers that called you, include your business name, and honor STOP.

pages.label: Service businesses
pages.title: AI virtual receptionist that answers FAQs and books on Google Calendar
pages.summary: Use an AI receptionist to answer common questions from a business-info sheet, check Google Calendar availability, book appointments, and log every conversation to Sheets.
steps: Write a short business-info sheet: hours, services, pricing ranges you approve, location, parking, and FAQs you want answered without a human.
Connect Google Calendar (the booking calendar) and a Google Sheet for conversation logs.
In n8n (or similar), wire an AI agent that reads the info sheet, checks free slots on Calendar, creates events when the caller confirms, and appends a row to Sheets.
Add a clear handoff: if the question is outside the sheet, or the caller asks for a human, route to your phone or email.
Test with a few sample chats before pointing real callers at it.

p: Tools: n8n + Google Calendar + Google Sheets + an AI model. A public n8n template covers an AI-powered virtual receptionist with Calendar booking and Sheets logging: https://n8n.io/workflows/8326-create-an-ai-powered-virtual-receptionist-with-google-calendar-and-sheets/
Related pattern: missed-call reply and appointment booking with Twilio, Google and GPT-4o: https://n8n.io/workflows/20250-reply-to-missed-calls-and-book-appointments-with-twilio-google-and-gpt-4o/
Costs: see each vendor's current pricing page; we don't list prices we haven't verified.
Don't invent prices or policies in the AI answers — only allow what is on your approved info sheet.
If you add SMS or WhatsApp, follow TCPA and carrier rules: identify the business, honor STOP, and only message people who opted in or who contacted you first.
Keep a human handoff for edge cases, complaints, and anything medical, legal or financial.

pages.label: Retail
pages.title: Alert staff when a SKU drops below your reorder threshold
pages.summary: Watch an inventory sheet or POS export; when a SKU falls below the threshold you set, alert staff and optionally draft a supplier reorder email for approval.
steps: Keep live stock counts in a Google Sheet (or export SKUs nightly from your POS into one).
Add a reorder_threshold column per SKU and a supplier email column if you want drafted emails.
In n8n, Zapier or Make, schedule a check that finds rows where quantity is at or below the threshold.
Send a Slack/email alert to staff with SKU, quantity, and threshold.
Optionally draft a supplier email (do not auto-send until a human approves) listing items to reorder.

p: Tools: Google Sheets or POS export + n8n/Zapier/Make + email or Slack. Inventory-below-threshold alerts are a common small-business automation pattern (see https://useomniai.com/n8n-automation-ideas-small-business/).
Costs: see each vendor's current pricing page.
This is different from a restaurant inventory-variance alert (usage vs sales). Here you only care that on-hand quantity crossed a reorder line.
Don't auto-order from suppliers without a human check — bad counts create bad POs.
Tune thresholds after a week or two so you aren't flooded with false alerts.

pages.title: Send reservation reminders that cut restaurant no-shows
pages.summary: Text or email each guest a reminder the day before and a few hours before their booking, with one-tap confirm or cancel, and free cancelled tables for the waitlist.

Track no-show rate weekly to see if the reminders help.

Don't send duplicate reminders if your booking platform already sends its own.

pages.label: Any local business
pages.title: Ask every customer for a Google review automatically (without review gating)
pages.summary: When a job or visit is marked complete, send every customer the same short review request with your Google review link, plus one reminder. Ask everyone, not just happy customers, and never offer a reward for the review.
steps: Get your review link from your Google Business Profile (the "Ask for reviews" or share-review-form option).
Trigger on a completed job, paid invoice or finished appointment in your booking, POS or field-service app via Zapier, Make or n8n.
Wait a few hours (or until the next morning), then text or email one short message with the link. Use the same message for every customer.
If there's no review after 3–5 days, send one reminder, then stop.
Log who was asked and when in a Google Sheet so nobody gets asked twice for the same visit.
Pair this with the review-reply recipe so every new review gets a timely, approved response.

p: Tools: your booking/POS/field app + Zapier/Make/n8n + SMS or email + a Google Sheet. Costs: see each vendor's current pricing page.

ul: Don't filter who gets asked. Google's policy says merchants may not "discourage or prohibit negative reviews, or selectively solicit positive reviews from customers". A "Did you love us? Yes → Google, No → private form" flow is exactly that.
No incentives. Google prohibits offering payment, discounts or free goods or services in exchange for a review, and the FTC's rule bans incentives conditioned on a positive review.
Never let AI write reviews for customers or staff. The FTC rule prohibits fake reviews, including AI-generated ones, and reviews by insiders who hide their connection.
Text only customers who gave you their number, identify your business and honor STOP replies.

p: Google Maps user-generated content policy (fake engagement) — https://support.google.com/contributionpolicy/answer/7400114

pages.summary: Turn on your invoicing tool's built-in reminders first. Then add a simple schedule (before due, on the due date, a week late) and have AI draft a personal note for anything older than 30 days that you approve before it goes out.
steps: Check your invoicing tool first. Stripe, for example, can email reminders when a one-off invoice hasn't been fully paid; QuickBooks, Xero and most field-service apps have similar settings. Turn those on before building anything.
If your tool can't do it, trigger on new invoices into a Google Sheet (invoice number, customer, amount, due date, payment link) with Zapier, Make or n8n.
Schedule friendly reminders: 3 days before the due date, on the due date, and 7 days after. Each one includes the amount, the invoice number and the payment link.
Stop the sequence the moment the invoice is marked paid (check status before every send).
At 30 days overdue, have AI draft a short personal note from the owner for review, not an automatic send.
Review the overdue list weekly and call your biggest balances yourself.

p: Tools: your invoicing tool (Stripe, QuickBooks, Xero, Jobber, Housecall Pro) + Zapier/Make/n8n + email. Costs: see each vendor's current pricing page.

pages.label: Clinics
pages.title: Cut clinic no-shows with a layered appointment reminder sequence
pages.summary: Send a booking confirmation, then reminders about 48–72 hours out, 24 hours out (with confirm/reschedule), and a short same-day logistics text. Keep SMS to date, time and clinic name—no diagnoses—and use a vendor that will sign a BAA.
steps: Confirm how your practice management or EHR already sends reminders. Turn on built-in reminders first if they cover confirmation and day-before texts; only add Zapier/Make/n8n for gaps.
Collect mobile numbers and written consent for appointment texts at registration. Document channel preferences and honor STOP and reasonable confidential-communication requests.

Build a layered cadence keyed to the live schedule: immediate booking confirmation (date, time, location or telehealth link, how to reschedule); a 48–72 hour reminder; a 24-hour two-way confirm/reschedule text; a short same-day logistics text 2–4 hours before.
Keep every unencrypted SMS minimal: patient first name optional, clinic name, date/time, confirm or reschedule instructions. No diagnoses, results, procedure details or clinical notes.
Stop the sequence when the visit is cancelled, rescheduled or completed. Sync status from the schedule before every send so you never remind for a dead slot.
After a no-show, send one polite rebook link and create a staff task—no blame language. Review no-show and confirmation rates monthly.

p: Tools: your practice management/EHR or booking calendar + a HIPAA-ready messaging vendor (with a signed BAA) and/or Zapier/Make/n8n + SMS/email. Costs: see each vendor's current pricing page.

ul: HHS OCR treats appointment reminders as part of treatment, so a separate authorization is not required—but you still must use reasonable safeguards and limit what you disclose.
On answering machines or shared phones, leave only what is needed to confirm the appointment (for example clinic name and callback number), not clinical detail.
If a patient asks for an alternate contact method or location, honor reasonable requests.
Text only numbers you have consent for, identify the clinic, and honor STOP. Prefer a vendor with a Business Associate Agreement rather than a consumer SMS app.
This is operational guidance, not legal advice—have your privacy officer review templates before launch.

pages.label: Retail
pages.title: Send one abandoned-cart SMS (with proper SMS consent)
pages.summary: When a shopper who already opted into SMS leaves items in cart, send one reminder within 48 hours with a link back to checkout. Use double opt-in, disclose cart reminders in your signup terms, and never collect payment by text.
steps: Turn on SMS signup at checkout and on-site with clear disclosure that the program includes cart or checkout reminders. Use double opt-in (subscriber confirms by text) before any abandoned-cart send.
Update your mobile terms and privacy policy to say you track abandoned carts (for example via cookies or your cart plugin) and may send SMS cart reminders to opted-in subscribers.
In Shopify, WooCommerce or your cart tool, trigger when a cart or checkout is abandoned and the shopper is an active SMS subscriber (opted in before abandonment).
Send exactly one SMS per abandonment event, within 48 hours. Include your business name, a short cart nudge, a direct link to the cart/checkout page, and STOP instructions.
Do not complete the purchase by text, collect card data by SMS, or accept a keyword as payment approval—the customer must pay on your site.
Log consent, send time and STOP replies. Keep sends inside quiet hours for the shopper's time zone, and stop if they opt out.

p: Tools: your ecommerce cart (Shopify, WooCommerce, etc.) + an SMS platform that supports double opt-in and abandoned-cart flows, or Zapier/Make/n8n as a bridge. Costs: see each vendor's current pricing page.

ul: Abandoned-cart texts are marketing under the TCPA when sent with autodialers—get prior express written consent, keep records, and honor STOP in any reasonable wording.
US carriers commonly require double opt-in, one SMS per abandoned-cart event, and send within 48 hours for this use case.
Disclose cart reminders in the signup CTA/terms and explain cart tracking in the privacy policy.
Don't text people who only browsed or who never opted into SMS. Don't stack email + three SMS nudges for the same cart if your SMS flow already used its one allowed message.
This is compliance hygiene, not legal advice—confirm current carrier and state rules with your counsel or SMS vendor.

pages.label: Contractors
pages.title: Reply to new website leads within minutes, automatically
pages.summary: When a quote or contact form comes in, send the lead a short personal-sounding reply right away, ping the owner or estimator by text, and log the lead in a sheet or CRM. An AI step can draft the reply from the form details, but keep it to facts you can stand behind.
steps: List every place leads arrive: website form, Google Business Profile messages, Facebook, Angi/Thumbtack-style platforms. Start with your own website form; it is the easiest to connect.
Trigger on each new form submission in Zapier, Make or n8n (or your form tool's built-in notifications).

Add an AI step that drafts a 3–5 sentence reply using only the form fields: thank them by name, restate the job they described, say when a person will call (for example "today before 5 PM"), and offer a booking link if you have one. Tell the AI not to quote prices, promise dates or guess at scope.
Send the reply from a real business address that people can answer, with your business name in the From line.
At the same moment, text or Slack the owner or on-call estimator with the lead's name, phone, job type and a link to the record, so a human calls back fast.
Log every lead (time received, time replied, source, status) in Google Sheets or your CRM, and review weekly which leads went cold and how fast you actually called back.

p: Tools: your website form (or form builder), Zapier/Make/n8n, an AI step (for example the OpenAI or Claude action in your automation tool), email, and an SMS or Slack alert for the team. Costs: see each vendor's current pricing page.

ul: Speed matters: Harvard Business Review research on online sales leads found most companies are not responding nearly fast enough to inquiries. An instant acknowledgment buys time, but a human callback is what wins the job.

A one-to-one reply to someone who just asked you for a quote is a response to their request. If you later add them to promotional emails, the FTC's CAN-SPAM rules apply: accurate From line, honest subject, your postal address, and a working opt-out honored within 10 business days.
Don't let the AI invent prices, availability, licensing or warranty terms. Keep those in a human-approved template.
Only text the lead if they gave their number for that purpose; otherwise reply by email and let your team call.
Watch for spam form fills before they trigger alerts: add a captcha or honeypot field to the form.

p: Harvard Business Review: The Short Life of Online Sales Leads (Oldroyd, McElheran, Elkington, March 2011) — https://hbr.org/2011/03/the-short-life-of-online-sales-leads

pages.label: Any local business
pages.title: Capture receipts by photo or email and file them for your bookkeeper
pages.summary: Give everyone one way to submit receipts (a forwarding email address or a phone upload), let an AI step read the vendor, date, amount and category, file the image in a dated folder, and add a row to a sheet your bookkeeper reviews. A person approves categories before anything is posted to the books.
steps: Check what your accounting software already does. Many bookkeeping apps include receipt capture by mobile photo or email forwarding; turn that on first and only automate the gaps.
Create one intake path: a dedicated email address (for example receipts@yourbusiness) or a shared phone-upload folder. Tell staff to submit every receipt the same day.
Trigger on each new email attachment or uploaded image in Zapier, Make or n8n.
Add an AI or OCR step that extracts vendor, date, total, tax and payment method, and suggests a category from your chart of accounts. Flag anything it can't read clearly.
Rename and save the original image or PDF into a folder by year and month (for example Receipts/2026/10) so it is easy to find later.
Append a row to a review sheet with the extracted fields, a link to the file and a status column. Your bookkeeper confirms or fixes the category, then records it in the books.

p: Tools: email or a phone upload app, Google Drive/Dropbox/OneDrive, Zapier/Make/n8n with an OCR or AI document step, Google Sheets, and your accounting software. Costs: see each vendor's current pricing page.

ul: The IRS says supporting documents such as sales slips, paid bills, invoices, receipts, deposit slips and canceled checks support the entries in your books and on your tax return, and suggests organizing them by year and type of income or expense.
Keep the original file, not just the extracted numbers. AI extraction can misread totals or dates, so a person should review before posting.

Retention depends on your situation. The IRS's general rule for income-tax records is 3 years, with longer periods in specific cases (for example 6 years for substantially underreported income and 7 years for bad-debt or worthless-securities claims). Ask your tax preparer what applies to you.
Receipts can include card digits and personal details. Store them in a business account with limited sharing, not a personal phone album.
This is a workflow guide, not tax advice.
